questions.question: For the FeCoCrNi-based HEA produced via SPS, does the protective spinel oxide layer formed at 900°C reduce wear depth more effectively than at 700°C, and does the σ-phase formation degrade wear performance if the temperature exceeds 850°C where the oxide layer stabilizes?
questions.rationale: Answering this determines the operational temperature window for this specific SPS microstructure. If the σ-phase or oxide instability at high temperatures negates wear resistance, process parameters must be tuned to avoid these regimes.
questions.decision_use: Define the maximum safe operating temperature for reciprocating wear applications to prevent sudden failure due to oxide layer breakdown or phase degradation.
answer_requirements: Compare wear depth and oxide morphology (XRD/SEM) at 700°C, 800°C, 850°C, and 900°C under identical reciprocating load.
Quantify the correlation between σ-phase fraction and wear depth at temperatures >850°C.
evidence_spans: The decrease in wear depth proves the protection of the underlying material by tribo-oxidation and the formaton of a stable oxide film.
The additional maxima can be assigned to a spinel (structure type MgAl 2 O 4 ). The intensity of the diffraction peaks increases for the sample tested at a maximum temperature of 900 °C.

questions.question: For this SPS-processed HEA, is the coefficient of friction reduction at 900°C solely due to the protective spinel oxide layer, or does the specific cooling rate (150 K/min) influence the oxide adherence and thus the COF value of 0.85?
questions.rationale: Distinguishing between the mechanism of the oxide layer and the influence of the cooling rate on microstructure/oxide adhesion is critical. If cooling rate is the dominant factor, altering the thermal history could optimize COF without changing composition.
questions.decision_use: Determine whether to prioritize optimizing sintering/cooling protocols or alloy composition to achieve lower friction in high-temperature reciprocating applications.
answer_requirements: Measure COF and oxide adhesion (scratch test/SEM) for samples SPS processed with controlled cooling rates (e.g., 50 K/min, 300 K/min) versus the native 150 K/min.
Correlate oxide adherence strength with COF values.
evidence_spans: The wear resistance under reciprocating wear conditions increases at elevated temperatures due to the formation of a protective oxide layer under atmospherical conditions.
